memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: On the Sabbath day, make an offering of two lambs a year old without defect, together with its drink offering and a grain offering of two-tenths of an ephah of the finest flour mixed with olive oil. This is the burnt offering for every Sabbath, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its drink offering. - Num 28:9-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
On the Sabbath, the offerings were doubled. The day of rest was also a day of increased worship, marking it as set apart and holy. God did not intend the Sabbath merely as a break from labour, but as a day devoted more fully to Him. Rest and worship went hand in hand.

This teaches us something about true rest. The Sabbath was not simply about stopping work; it was about turning to God. The added offerings showed that the day belonged especially to the Lord. Rest without God is incomplete; the deepest rest is found in drawing near to Him and delighting in His presence.

We should note that sincere Christians hold differing views on how the Sabbath applies today, and we need not settle those debates here. What is clear is that the principle of regular rest and worship remains a gift from God. He knows we need rhythms of rest, and He invites us to find our rest in Him.

The truest Sabbath rest is found in Christ, who invites all who are weary and burdened to come to Him and find rest for their souls (Matt 11:28). He is our rest, the fulfilment of every Sabbath. In Him we cease striving to earn God's favour and rest in what He has already accomplished. Come to Him, and find the rest your soul was made for.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you find true rest in God, or only in stopping your work?
2. How does Christ offer the rest your soul truly needs?
3. What rhythms of rest and worship might God be inviting you into?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You invite the weary to come to You and find rest. Teach me to cease my striving and rest in Your finished work, delighting in You as the true Sabbath for my soul. Amen.
